stem: The compound interest on a principal sum P at 10% per annum for 3 years exceeds the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for the same period by Rs 310. A creditor is owed this principal P and will receive it as a lump sum 3 years from now. At a discount rate of 10% per annum, what is the present value of that future receipt today?  [Given: (1.1)^3 = 1.331]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Correctly back-computing P = Rs 10,000 but returning P itself instead of its present value ignores the discounting step, solving the wrong quantity.
Discounting P = 10,000 for only 2 years instead of 3 gives 10,000 / (1.1)^2 = 10,000 / 1.21 = Rs 8,264, an off-by-one period error.
Using simple-interest discounting PV = P / (1 + nr) = 10,000 / (1 + 0.10 x 3) = 10,000 / 1.30 = Rs 7,692 instead of compound discounting.

explanation: This two-step problem first uses the CI-SI difference formula to recover P, then discounts P at compound interest to find today's value. CI - SI over n years = P[(1+r)^n - 1 - nr]. For n=3, r=0.10: 310 = P x 0.031, so P = 10,000. PV = 10,000 / (1.1)^3 = 10,000 / 1.331 = Rs 7,513.

explanation_sections.punchline: The hidden relationship is CI - SI = P[(1+r)^n - 1 - nr] - recover P from this, then apply compound PV discounting.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: CI - SI = P[(1+r)^n - 1 - nr]. Step 1 - CI-SI back-calc: 310 = P[1.331 - 1 - 0.30] = P x 0.031, so P = 10,000. Step 2 - PV formula: PV = P/(1+r)^n = 10,000/1.331 = Rs 7,513. The same hint (1.1)^3 = 1.331 serves both steps.
explanation_sections.lesson: CI - SI = P[(1+r)^n - 1 - nr] is the vault formula for this back-calculation; the three-year version adds one more term than the two-year r^2 shortcut.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. Two distinct steps: CI-SI inversion then compound PV. Trap: option 2 = P not PV; option 3 = wrong n in discount; option 4 = simple not compound discount.
